The app is **makemore**, a Python service that builds a character-level bigram language model from a training corpus. It exists to show that counting the next-character frequencies and training a neural net on those same counts converge on the same model — the code proves the neural net is not magic but a differentiable way to arrive at the counted table.

The three files work together: `bigram_counts.py` builds a 27×27 counts matrix (26 letters plus a `.` boundary marker) from the names file; `nn_bigram.py` trains a one-layer neural net to learn that same matrix via gradient descent; `sampling.py` turns the learned weights into probability distributions and walks them to generate new plausible names.

The only dependencies are imports between these files — `nn_bigram.py` imports `build_counts` from `bigram_counts.py`, and `sampling.py` does the same. There are no data stores, external topics, or services beyond the single service `svc:makemore`. The risk section lists no single points of failure or circular dependencies.

**Root overview:** The request flows through three files in `svc:makemore`: first, `bigram_counts.py` reads `names.txt` and builds the counts matrix; second, `nn_bigram.py` calls `build_counts` and trains the neural net on those counts; third, `sampling.py` calls `build_counts` again and uses the matrix to sample names. No data store or external topic is involved.

**Next concept to explore:** the `build_counts` function in `bigram_counts.py`, which is the shared foundation both the neural net and the sampler rely on.

The product flow works like this. A user's request starts at the `svc:gateway`, an Express server in `index.ts` (not read this turn) that sets up routes. The gateway forwards API calls to the right service through `http` edges: orders go to `svc:orders` (FastAPI in `routes.py` (not read this turn) and `main.py` (not read this turn)), payments to `svc:payments` (Express at `index.js` (not read this turn)), invoices to `svc:invoices` (Java at `InvoiceController.java` (not read this turn)), and shipments to `svc:shipping` (Go at `main.go` (not read this turn)). The `svc:edge` provides default config via an `/api/` route edge on `edge/default.conf`.

A new order gets persisted to PostgreSQL in `db.py` (not read this turn) (edges `e13`, `e14`, `e15` for reads/writes to `ds:postgres`). The order event is published to the `topic:order.created` Redis broker (edge `e10`) and consumed by `svc:notifications`, `svc:inventory`, and `svc:shipping` — each as a `queue_consume` on that topic. Payments use their own `db.js` (not read this turn) for store writes (edges `e16`, `e17`, `e18`).
